*The layers of the user model, in `django/contrib/auth/base_user.py` and `django/contrib/auth/models.py`.*
`AbstractBaseUser.is_active` is a class attribute, true, so a model that does not make it a field has every user active (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser`).

`BaseUserManager.get_by_natural_key`, a `get` on the same field, is how `ModelBackend` finds the user a login names ([Authenticating: `authenticate` and the backends](authenticating.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:BaseUserManager.get_by_natural_key`).

`AbstractBaseUser.clean` passes the username through `AbstractBaseUser.normalize_username`, which applies Unicode's NFKC normalization so that, as the documentation puts it, visually identical characters with different code points count as identical (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.normalize_username`, `docs/topics/auth/customizing.txt`).

`AbstractBaseUser.clean` passes the username through `AbstractBaseUser.normalize_username`, which applies Unicode's NFKC normalization so that, as the documentation puts it, visually identical characters with different code points count as identical (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.normalize_username`, `docs/topics/auth/customizing.txt`).

It keeps the raw password in `AbstractBaseUser._password` so that, a comment says, it can be passed to `password_changed` after the model is saved: `AbstractBaseUser.save` saves, then calls `password_changed` if `_password` is set, and clears it ([Password validation: `validate_password` and the validators](password-validation.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.save`).

The setter calls `set_password`, clears `_password`, since by its comment a hash upgrade is not a password change, and saves the `password` field alone ([Password hashing: `make_password` and the hashers](hashers.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.check_password`).

`AbstractBaseUser.set_unusable_password` stores `make_password(None)`, a string beginning with `"!"` that no password matches, and `AbstractBaseUser.has_usable_password` tells it with `is_password_usable` (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser.set_unusable_password`).

`BaseUserManager.normalize_email` strips an address that has an `"@"` and lowercases what follows the last one, leaving the local part as it was; a missing address becomes `""` (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:BaseUserManager.normalize_email`).
It sets the password with `make_password`, not `set_password`, so no `password_changed` follows (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:UserManager._create_user_object`).

`PermissionsMixin` adds `is_superuser` and two many-to-many fields, `groups` to the group model and `user_permissions` to `Permission`, each with the related name `"user_set"` (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:PermissionsMixin`).
`AbstractUser.email_user` calls `send_mail` with the user's address (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:AbstractUser`).

The username is validated by `UnicodeUsernameValidator`, which allows word characters and `"."`, `"@"`, `"+"` and `"-"`; `ASCIIUsernameValidator` is the same pattern with the ASCII flag, and refuses "tomás" (`django/contrib/auth/validators.py`).
`User` adds to `AbstractUser` only a `Meta` that sets the swappable option to `"AUTH_USER_MODEL"` (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:User`).
Any two are equal, every one hashes to 1, and `int` of one raises `TypeError`, asking whether it is being used in place of a user (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:AnonymousUser`).

`get_user_model` asks the registry for the model `AUTH_USER_MODEL` names with `require_ready=False` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user_model`), which needs only the applications loaded, not all their models, and imports the named application's models itself if they are not yet (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.get_model`).

`get_user_model` asks the registry for the model `AUTH_USER_MODEL` names with `require_ready=False` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user_model`), which needs only the applications loaded, not all their models, and imports the named application's models itself if they are not yet (`django/apps/registry.py:Apps.get_model`).
`AuthConfig.ready` calls `get_user_model`, so a wrong value stops `django.setup` (`django/contrib/auth/apps.py:AuthConfig.ready`).

The backends, the forms, the views, changepassword and the mod_wsgi handler keep the class they got at import as `UserModel` (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:UserModel`); only a receiver of `setting_changed`, which `override_settings` sends, binds the five again (`django/test/signals.py:user_model_swapped`).

When the setting names another model, `User`'s `Options.swapped` is that name (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.swapped`): migrate makes no table for it, the registry's lists leave it out (`django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.get_models`), and its manager refuses to be read ([The options: what a model keeps as `_meta`](../models/options.md)).

The documentation asks that it be set before the first migrate (`docs/topics/auth/customizing.txt`).

It makes an instance with no arguments, and requires that `REQUIRED_FIELDS` be a list or tuple (`"auth.E001"`) and not hold `USERNAME_FIELD` (`"auth.E002"`); that the username field be unique, or the only field of a unique constraint with no condition, an error (`"auth.E003"`) when `AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS` is `ModelBackend` alone and otherwise a warning (`"auth.W004"`); and that `is_anonymous` and `is_authenticated` not be callable (`"auth.C009"`, `"auth.C010"`, critical) (`django/contrib/auth/checks.py:check_user_model`).
